transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess… what brings me in is I’ve been having these thoughts where, not that I’ve made some plan or anything, but I catch myself thinking it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up. And then I’ll be at work, ringing somebody up for batteries or socks or whatever, and it just kind of hits me how strange it is to be standing there smiling at people while thinking that.
Did these thoughts start after something stressful happened in your life?

I don’t know if it was one thing stressful, exactly. I mean, work is always kind of… people come in mad about coupons or returns, and you stand there taking it, and then you go home and the house is quiet. But I came in because I keep catching myself thinking maybe it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up. I haven’t made a plan to hurt myself or anything like that. It’s more like the thought just shows up, and then I’m thinking about it while doing normal stuff, which feels… wrong, I guess.
Did these thoughts begin after a specific stressful event or major change in your life?

Not really a specific thing, no. I mean, there’s always stress—work, customers, coming home and everything being quiet—but I can’t point to, like, one event where it started. I came in because I keep catching myself thinking it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up. I haven’t made any plan to hurt myself or anything. It just kind of… shows up.
Have you been feeling down or depressed معظم الأيام?

Yeah… most days, I think. It’s like after that burst of energy I had wore off, somebody just pulled the plug on me. I’d sit at the kitchen table with my coffee and just stare at it, and then I’d start feeling empty, and kind of ashamed too. Funny thing is I don’t even drink fancy coffee—just the cheap stuff from the big can—but I’d sit there like it was supposed to tell me what to do next.
Before you started feeling this down, was there a period when you felt unusually energetic or up compared with your normal self?

Yeah… there was a stretch right after I got fired where I felt weirdly fired up, like, “Fine, I’ll show all of you.” I had all this energy in me, but it wasn’t exactly happy energy. I was getting real short with people, too—like snapping at folks over nothing at the coffee shop. Which is embarrassing, because I go there enough that they know my order, you know, and then I’m the guy acting like the lid being loose is some personal insult.
During that fired-up stretch, did you need less sleep than usual?

Yeah, I did. There were a few nights where I only slept, I don’t know, two or three hours, and then I’d get up like I’d slept a full night. Like I had a full tank, no reason to slow down. Which isn’t normal for me—usually if I sleep like that, I’m useless the next day. But then I’d be up, moving around, making coffee, thinking I should be doing something… and then I’d get distracted by, like, reorganizing junk drawers or whatever.
During that fired-up stretch, did you feel unusually confident or like you could do things other people couldn’t?

Yeah, I guess I did. For a while there I honestly thought I could walk into pretty much any store in the district and run it better than the managers they had. Like getting fired had somehow made me the expert, which sounds ridiculous saying it now. I’d be standing in an aisle somewhere noticing how they stocked the batteries or whatever and thinking, “See, I’d fix this place in a week.”
During that fired-up stretch, were you doing a lot more activities or projects than usual?

Yeah, definitely. I was kind of bouncing all over the place—job applications, then I’d stop and start sketching these woodworking projects like I was suddenly gonna build a whole set of shelves, then I’d go back and rewrite my résumé for the tenth time. 

I’d barely sit still long enough to finish one thing before I was onto the next. I even found myself looking up types of wood, which is funny because my garage is mostly full of old paint cans and stuff I’ve been meaning to take to the dump for, I don’t know, years. But yeah… I was doing a lot more than usual, just not finishing much.
During that fired-up period, were you hospitalized because of how you were acting?

Hospitalized? No… I mean, I don’t think so. I didn’t go to a hospital for it. I remember people saying I was acting weird, but that’s different, you know? My sister once had to go in for her gallbladder and that whole waiting room was a nightmare—those plastic chairs are like they’re designed by somebody who’s never sat down before.

But for me, no, I wasn’t checked in anywhere or anything like that.
During that fired-up stretch, did it cause serious problems in your life, like getting into major trouble at work, with money, or with other people?

Yeah… it did, I guess. Not like I got arrested or anything, but my life got kind of messy. I fell behind on bills because I’d keep meaning to handle them and then I’d be off doing something else, or convinced I had some better plan for fixing everything.

And with work—well, looking for work—I missed callbacks and appointments, which is stupid because I needed a job. I’d start strong, then just lose the thread. My place got sloppy too, like regular home stuff just wasn’t happening. Dishes, mail, laundry… the kind of stuff you think you can just buckle down and do, but I couldn’t seem to make myself keep it together by willpower alone.
About that fired-up stretch after you got fired, did it last at least four days in a row?

Yeah, more than four days. It was… I’d say close to three weeks after I got fired. Time got kind of blurry in there, because I wasn’t keeping track the way I normally would—like I’d look up and realize the trash pickup already came and I still had the bins sitting by the side door.

But yeah, it wasn’t just a weekend or a couple days. It went on for weeks, about three.
